title: Halcyon Labs - Discovery: Migration OpenAI to Dedicated
summary: Initial discovery focused on migrating inference from public APIs (OpenAI) to Redwood Dedicated. Key concerns: eval parity, latency and cost tradeoffs, compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks, VPC/KMS requirements, rollout strategy and benchmarks. Agreed next steps: run 1-week benchmark on sample workloads, share Dedicated pricing and security docs, schedule SE-led technical deep dive for infra team.
next_steps: Ari to send Dedicated pricing and capacity options (by 2026-08-13)
Samir to share benchmark plan and script (by 2026-08-14)
Halcyon to provide sample prompt set and eval metrics (by 2026-08-14)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ari Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Halcyon Head of ML), Carlos Rivera (CTO), Priya Desai (Eng Manager)

Summary:
(Automated) Quick notes — some words may be off, transcription medium quality.

[00:00:00] Ari: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ari, AE at Redwood. Samir's our SE, he'll cover the deeper infra bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Maya: Good, thanks. Appreciate you making time. We're evaluating moving a bunch of inference off OpenAI into something more predictable — interested in Redwood Dedicated and possibly Private later.
[00:00:22] Ari: Great, that's exactly what we do. Quick agenda: understand current stack, workloads and metrics, constraints, and then talk about compatibility and a potential pilot.
[00:00:33] Carlos: Sounds good. Quick context: we're doing chat summaries, legal doc parsing and embeddings for search. Latency SLO is 400 ms p95 for summaries, embeddings are batch off-line. We've been on OpenAI for 9 months. Costs are ramping and we have compliance asks.
[00:00:50] Priya: Also want to understand if eval parity is realistic — we ran internal evals vs OpenAI and saw small delta but want to avoid regressions.
[00:00:59] Samir: Totally, that's a common concern. A lot of our customers move from public API to Dedicated and run side-by-side evals. We have tooling to reproduce prompt/temperature + sampling. Important to capture prompt engineering differences and tokenization quirks between providers.
[00:01:15] Maya: Yeah, tokenization and system prompts caused some drift with Anthropic too, so we want to be careful.
[00:01:22] Ari: One quick Q: are you running any custom inference stacks like vLLM or TGI internally?
[00:01:28] Maya: We experimented with v L M on-prem for a month — mainly to reduce cost for embeddings but it got tricky at scale. T G I we used for prototyping. Production has been OpenAI.
[00:01:39] Samir: Good to know — compatibility with vLLM/TGI matters because many teams have evaluation harnesses built around them. Our Dedicated runtime supports the same model families and we provide model artifacts and config that are compatible with vLLM/TGI in most cases, but there are kernel/quantization differences to watch for.
[00:01:56] Carlos: When you say "compatible" — do you mean we can drop-in our vLLM workloads or do we need to re-run a lot of tuning?
[00:02:05] Samir: In practice, some tuning. Things like quantization profiles, layer-fusing and attention kernel selection can change latency and small output behaviors. For eval parity we recommend running a 1-week benchmark where we replay production prompt sets against both OpenAI and Redwood Dedicated. We capture BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine and business metrics.
[00:02:26] Priya: Okay, what about KV cache and streaming behavior? Our use case relies on prefix caching for multi-turn chat.
[00:02:34] Samir: We have continuous KV cache, similar semantics to vLLM, but the runtime is optimized differently. Streaming is supported and you can tune chunk sizes and buffer timings on Dedicated. There may be slight differences in timing which can affect p95 latencies, but we tune for latency SLOs at customer level.
[00:02:50] Maya: Security — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and customer-managed keys. Is that all available?
[00:02:58] Ari: Yes. Dedicated comes with audit logs, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC, and for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations. We can share our compliance packet.
[00:03:10] Carlos: Any examples of data residency or region controls? We have EU customers so data can’t leave region.
[00:03:16] Ari: Hosted has region controls for EU, but for stricter needs Dedicated in a region or Private VPC is the route — you control network egress.
[00:03:24] Maya: On performance: our summaries hit ~350 tokens occasionally, do you support long-context models with efficient kernels?
[00:03:31] Samir: Yes, we support long-context models and have custom kernel selection for 4k-32k contexts. We also recommend prefix caching and batching policies to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency.
[00:03:43] Carlos: Can we get consistent model versions? We want to pin to a verified artifact for a quarter.
[00:03:48] Ari: Definitely — Dedicated lets you pin model versions and we support rollout policies and canary deploys.
[00:03:55] Priya: About cost — rough delta vs OpenAI, what do customers see?
[00:04:00] Ari: It depends. For high-volume workloads Dedicated often reduces unit cost by 30-60% depending on batching and quantization. We can model it if you share token counts and QPS.
[00:04:12] Maya: We have roughly 3M tokens/day for generation and 1M for embeddings. QPS spikes to 120 peak, sustained 40.
[00:04:23] Samir: That's useful. We'll propose an autoscale config and reserved pool size in the benchmark plan.
[00:04:29] Carlos: How about fallback strategies? If Dedicated capacity hits limits, do you have hosted fallback?
[00:04:36] Ari: Yes — smart routing policies let you failover to other capacity tiers or regions; you can configure cost vs latency tradeoffs. For mission-critical flows we often set a fallback to a lower-cost variant or hosted API with rate limits.
[00:04:48] Maya: Any managed eval tooling? We run regression tests nightly and we'd like alerts on quality regressions after model or infra changes.
[00:04:56] Samir: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring, and you can wire your eval harness to trigger regression alerts. We can integrate with your CI to block rollouts if metrics drop.
[00:05:08] Priya: For the POC, what's typical length and what do you need from us?
[00:05:14] Ari: Typical POC is 1-2 weeks of side-by-side benchmarking. We need your prompt set, sample traffic or a replay harness, target eval metrics, and a contact on infra for network setup. We'll provide a dedicated pool and the benchmark scripts.
[00:05:27] Maya: Network — we have a VPC with strict egress, can Dedicated sit inside our VPC?
[00:05:33] Samir: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; for even stricter compliance we can discuss Private where control plane is customer-managed.
[00:05:42] Carlos: If we go Private later, how different is onboarding? Time to production?
[00:05:47] Ari: Private has a longer lead time — usually 6-10 weeks for full on-prem or VPC-private control plane depending on integration. Dedicated can be spun up in days to a couple of weeks.
[00:05:58] Priya: Any gotchas with tokenization differences vs OpenAI? We saw odd truncation once migrating a system prompt.
[00:06:05] Samir: Tokenization variants exist between model vendors; when we onboard models we provide tokenization parity checks and recommend canonicalization of system prompts. Also check max sequence lengths and how EOS tokens are handled.
[00:06:18] Maya: We use a few models family X/Y — will you support both?
[00:06:22] Samir: We support the mainstream family variants; if you have a specific model ID share it and we'll validate. For vLLM/TGI artifacts we can often repackage or provide conversion guidance.
[00:06:33] Ari: Ok, let's go through concrete benchmarks — Samir, can you outline the plan?
[00:06:37] Samir: Sure. We'll run: 1) Latency p50/p95/p99 for summaries; 2) Output delta metrics (ROUGE/BLEU + human sample checks) vs OpenAI; 3) Embeddings cosine similarity and downstream retrieval A/B; 4) Cost estimate per 1M tokens with current batching profiles. We'll need the prompt sets, tokenization examples and sample traffic. We'll provide scripts to run locally or we'll run inside your VPC with a replay harness.
[00:07:03] Maya: Sounds good. Can you also include vLLM/TGI comparison notes? We tried vLM with cpu fallback issues.
[00:07:10] Samir: Yes — we'll include a section noting where performance differences come from: kernel choices, CUDA kernels, quantization levels. We'll also include guidance on whether to use an FP16 or quantized int8 profile.
[00:07:21] Carlos: One more on security: do you support customer-managed KMS for model keys and logs encryption?
[00:07:27] Ari: For Dedicated we support customer KMS for data at rest in many deployments; in Private you can plug HSM. We'll include specifics in the security packet.
[00:07:35] Priya: Who will be our contact for infra setup — for peering and network tests?
[00:07:39] Ari: Samir will be the SE lead; he'll coordinate with your infra.
[00:07:44] Samir: Yep, I'll set up a one-hour deep-dive with your infra and we can attempt a simple ping/traceroute and test replays.
[00:07:52] Maya: Timeline — we're aiming to decide by end of August. Does that fit the POC window?
[00:07:58] Ari: Yes, if we start the POC this week or next we can wrap benchmark and present results by late August.
[00:08:04] Carlos: Pricing ask — for Dedicated what are the commitment levels and overage policy?
[00:08:10] Ari: We offer reserved capacity monthly/annual; typical POC uses a short-term reserved pool with overage caps. For production we'll recommend a monthly commit and autoscale. I'll send the pricing tiers.
[00:08:22] Priya: How are model updates handled? If Redwood updates a model, do we get notified and can we pin?
[00:08:28] Samir: You can pin versions; we also provide notes on behavioral changes. For Dedicated we only update when the customer allows or requests a rollout.
[00:08:37] Maya: Any initial red flags from your side about our use case?
[00:08:40] Samir: Nothing major; the main work will be the side-by-side eval and network setup. We'll watch out for any bespoke tokenizers or pre/post-processing you have.
[00:08:50] Ari: Ok, quick recap and actions — Ari to send pricing and security packet, Samir to share benchmark scripts and schedule infra deep-dive, Halcyon to share sample prompt sets and current eval metrics.
[00:09:03] Carlos: Agreed. Thanks y'all.
[00:09:06] Maya: Thanks. Looking forward to the doc and scripts.
[00:09:10] Priya: Bye.
[00:09:12] Ari: Thanks everyone. End.

(End of transcript — some timestamps compressed for brevity)
